quizName: Hardest Questions in District of columbia Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: To get the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Buy a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all around your head and have no visible damage.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing that covers your arms and legs completely. Good protective gear includes a sturdy jacket, pants, boots that cover your ankles, and gloves.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you're planning to increase your speed.
Only when there is a lot of traffic.
Any time you plan on changing lanes.
Only if it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan on changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend into traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Not use turn signals unless you are riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Tell them what you plan to do using turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready to react to dangers.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, you can help others see you by:
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear brightly colored clothing, keep your headlight on all the time, and always use your turn signals.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothing should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever makes you most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Protect yourself while riding by wearing a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Others may be driving slowly while looking for a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars create several dangers. A driver might pull out without looking and hit you. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Encourage them to take roads that are not crowded.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have had too much to drink. Do whatever it takes to stop them, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Restricts the wearer's vision to the sides.
Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
Makes it more difficult for the wearer to control their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce the severity of a head injury.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet while riding greatly reduces your risk of serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not restrict your side vision.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and keep your motorcycle upright. Move across the surface as slowly as possible.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: As part of your regular scanning routine.
They are not helpful since you cannot control what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: As part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will stay in your lane.
It is safe because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you start a turn or curve.

questions.question: Should you check your mirrors regularly?

options.text: Yes, as part of your regular scanning routine.
No, because other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, as part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: For your safety, you need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your specific motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual as your main source of information about your motorcycle. It contains details about how your motorcycle works, its features, and maintenance needs.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: As much as a face shield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: What type of soles should motorcycle riding footwear have?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy riding boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with soles that are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Why should a rider wear a leather jacket?

options.text: It is too warm to wear while riding.
It protects you in a crash.
You should not wear one while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket while riding for protection. In warm weather, leather jackets can help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: Why are turn signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are small.
They alert other drivers to your intentions.
Use them only if other vehicles are nearby.
They are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to your intentions.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are vulnerable, so use your turn signals to warn others of your plans. Always use them when you change lanes or turn, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: What is the best source of information for your specific motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Read your owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles give the best protection. Laced boots work best. If your laces are long, tuck them in before riding so they don't get caught.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-high boots, and durable gloves. These items protect you. A baseball cap is not enough protection.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are typically made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel. The front brake provides more stopping power.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: By comparing it to another tire

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire can look fine even if it is under-inflated, so you cannot rely on looking at it.
